bottleneck.description: GEO Ka/L-band broadband (combined with Inmarsat) facing aggressive substitution from Starlink LEO and Eutelsat OneWeb across aviation, maritime, and government verticals.

dependency.key_customers: Commercial aviation (Delta, JetBlue, United IFC), US DoD, maritime/government, Inmarsat enterprise base
dependency.key_suppliers: Boeing (ViaSat-3 satellite bus), Airbus (older fleet), SpaceX/ULA (launch), ST Engineering iDirect (ground)

editorial.notes: Viasat's ViaSat-3 GEO satellites deliver >1 Tbps per bird, and the Inmarsat acquisition (May 2023) consolidated L-band MSS for safety services. However, Starlink's 7,000+ LEO satellites have rapidly captured maritime/aviation broadband share, and Eutelsat OneWeb competes in multi-orbit enterprise. IFC/IFE customers (JetBlue, Delta, etc.) are actively dual-sourcing. Safety-of-life GMDSS L-band on Inmarsat is more sticky but represents a small share of revenue. Overall structurally LOW given clear, deployed substitutes.
